chunks: About a man who stays with another man while owing him a debt: may he eat from his food? He said: “Yes, he may eat from his food for three days, and after that he should not eat anything.”

key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: three days, the permitted time limit
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt owed by one person to another
key_terms.سَمَاعَةُ: Sama'ah, the narrator asking the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.شَيْئاً: anything at all beyond the stated limit
key_terms.طَعَامِهِ: his food, meaning the host's provision

ai.seo_question: Can a debtor eat from the food of the person to whom he owes money?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a debtor benefiting from the food of the one to whom he owes a debt. It permits eating for three days, but forbids continuing beyond that, indicating a limit so that the debt relationship does not become a means of improper benefit.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3705 - Sama'ah asked Abu Abdillah (as) about a man who stays with another man to whom he owes a debt. Is it permissible for him to eat from his food?
Imam (as) said: "Yes, he may eat from his food for three days, but after that, he should not eat anything."
